about: Maloof Wines is the work of Bee Maloof, a former aerospace engineer, and Ross Maloof, a longtime Philadelphia restaurant wine pro, joined now by Bee’s wife, Michelle McCaw. Founded in 2015, they have been based since 2019 at No Clos Radio, a vineyard and winery outside Forest Grove planted in the early 1970s. Alongside their single-vineyard bottlings they make a playful “comic” range of blends, and “Where Ya PJs At?” is the best known, a skin-contact wine built mostly on Pinot Gris.

The 2024 is about 75% Pinot Gris fermented on its skins, 15% Riesling pressed straight to barrel, and 10% skin-contact Gewürztraminer, all organically farmed. Pinot Gris has pinkish-grey skins, so a few days on them gives the wine its copper-salmon color and a light grip of tannin. Everything ferments with native yeasts and rests in neutral oak before being blended in spring and bottled unfined and unfiltered at a light 11.5% alcohol.
Expect a dry, bright, rosé-like wine with dried cherry, white peach, soft herbs and a cranberry-edged acidity, finishing clean and mineral.
facts: Skin-contact Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer; direct-pressed Riesling
